question: In one isolated GitHub-hosted synthetic run of the unchanged volume-mip-output profile at the baseline, is every page-visible same-origin source-read rejection a request whose Chromium NetLog URL request and HTTP/2 session and stream prove a relation to a GOAWAY or an HTTP/2 session boundary on that session?
hypothesis_under_test: H1 (not demonstrated): nginx ends the browser's HTTP/2 connection at keepalive_requests (default 1000, no directive in proxy/) with GOAWAY, and a stream sent past that boundary is surfaced to the page as a fetch rejection instead of being sent again on a new connection.
alternatives_kept_open: A1: the HTTP/2 connection closes without GOAWAY (reset, idle or lingering close); a session boundary without the request-limit relation.
A2: a server RST_STREAM on an accepted stream while the session stays open (INCOMPATIBLE).
A3: a renderer-side or interception-side rejection while the network request completed or never existed (INCOMPATIBLE or UNMAPPED).
A4: a new connection fails to establish after a boundary (UNMAPPED without an HTTP/2 session binding; raw NetLog kept for review).
observation_added: Chromium NetLog in Default capture mode for every Chromium the profile's test worker launches (one per test class), written under RUNNER_TEMP, flushed when the class cleanup closes the browser, kept on pass and on failure; a killed browser leaves a truncated file that analyze.py still parses.

Context-level requestfailed records for every page of every context (popups and direct report re-prints outside the guarded helper included): wall and monotonic time, method, query-redacted URL, failure text, Playwright request timing, context and page ordinals and the unittest test id; context and page creation and close, route registrations, test start, stop and outcome.

A generated test-only copy of proxy/nginx.conf.template with one registered logging block ($msec $pid $connection $connection_requests $http2 $server_protocol $remote_addr:$remote_port, method, uri, status, sizes, times, upstream status) written to a mounted directory, an info-level error log there, and the image's main-level stderr error log repeated; an entrypoint dump of nginx -V and nginx -T at container start with the Orthanc Basic credential redacted.
A NetLog preflight: one Chromium launch through the same hook on a data: URL before the stack, proving the switch, the closed file and the event type names on this runner.
unchanged: Product code, tests, assertions, messages, the guarded re-attempt helper, budgets, selection, the profile and every other profile, the production proxy template and its connection behavior (no keepalive, HTTP/2, timeout, buffer, listener, upstream or location setting), and the profile's own services.log access format.

decision_rules.rule: The run is analysable only when the restore, prepare and collect records passed, the post-profile HEAD is the registered baseline and no tracked file differs. Otherwise the result is INCONCLUSIVE and no statement about the hypothesis is made.

Page-visible failures count only when the observer recorded a Chromium launch with --log-net-log and --net-log-capture-mode=Default and the profile left its test log; otherwise INCONCLUSIVE. A NetLog is usable when its constants and events parse and it names HTTP2_SESSION, HTTP2_SESSION_SEND_HEADERS, HTTP2_SESSION_RECV_GOAWAY, HTTP2_SESSION_CLOSE, URL_REQUEST_START_JOB and REQUEST_ALIVE; rejections without a usable NetLog are INCONCLUSIVE.

A page-visible source-read rejection is a context-level requestfailed record whose failure text does not contain ERR_ABORTED, whose host is the profile origin (port 9443) and whose path starts with /instances/ or /api/, from any page and call path, including direct report re-prints outside the guarded helper. ERR_ABORTED records are the loader's own cancels. When the profile logged a transport text or a MIP_OUTPUT_TRANSPORT_FAILURE line but no such rejection was captured, the result is INCONCLUSIVE.

Each rejection is matched to the NetLog URL request with the same host, path and method that started within 1000 ms of Playwright's request startTime (without startTime: that ended within 5 s before to 1 s after the record). COMPATIBLE: the failed request is bound to an HTTP/2 session that received GOAWAY at most 5 s before the request ended and its stream id is above last_accepted_stream_id, or it got no stream on that session, or its accepted stream was still open when the session closed; or, without GOAWAY, it was active without response headers when its session closed within 1 s after it ended. INCOMPATIBLE: the NetLog request failed with a non-transport error, or completed without error while the page reported a failure, or failed on an accepted stream while its session stayed open after GOAWAY, or received a server RST_STREAM without a session boundary, or its session shows no GOAWAY or close near the failure. UNMAPPED: no failed NetLog request matches, the matching request was cancelled, no HTTP/2 session binding exists, GOAWAY lacks last_accepted_stream_id, or an unclosed NetLog ends within 2 s of the failure.

SUPPORTED only when at least one rejection exists and every rejection is COMPATIBLE. REJECTED when any rejection is INCOMPATIBLE. INCONCLUSIVE when a rejection is UNMAPPED and none is INCOMPATIBLE. PARTIAL when there is no rejection but connection boundaries occurred: a GOAWAY on an origin session, a NetLog restart after ERR_HTTP2_SERVER_REFUSED_STREAM or ERR_HTTP2_GOAWAY_FRAME, or an nginx HTTP/2 connection whose highest $connection_requests equals the effective keepalive_requests. INCONCLUSIVE when there is neither a rejection nor an observed boundary.

The native outcome, MIP_OUTPUT_TRANSPORT_FAILURE lines and guarded re-attempts are reported verbatim as existing instrumentation and never counted as detection. $connection_requests at keepalive_requests is corroboration only and never yields SUPPORTED by itself; no cause is inferred from request number 1000 alone. A run without a rejection does not resolve the main-01 failure; SUPPORTED describes this run only, and any correction needs its own reviewed unit.

The recheck classification must equal the hosted one and the manifest hashes must match the extracted files.
analysis.review: Every UNMAPPED or INCOMPATIBLE reason and every COMPATIBLE relation is checked against the raw NetLog lines, the diagnostic access and error logs and the effective configuration before any conclusion; PARTIAL or INCONCLUSIVE leaves main-01 blocked.

limits: Observer effect: NetLog writing and Python listeners add small latency and could change the probability of a boundary race.
One run may show no rejection (CI02 and several mutation jobs had none); that is PARTIAL or INCONCLUSIVE and does not resolve main-01.
NetLog event and parameter names are confirmed on the runner only by the preflight; an unexpected layout becomes UNMAPPED, and the raw sanitized NetLog stays available for review.

The browser reaches nginx through Docker port publishing (the access log shows the bridge gateway), so an nginx connection is matched to a NetLog session by answered stream paths and times, not by ports; corroboration only.

Default capture mode strips cookies and credentials; query values, JWTs, bearer and basic tokens, cookie and authorization headers and secret JSON fields are also redacted before upload; raw hashes are recorded and raw files are not uploaded.
The logging block repeats 'error_log /var/log/nginx/error.log notice;' as the stock nginx:1.27-alpine main-level value; the effective configuration dump shows the value actually in effect.
Local validation is pure: no browser, container, Docker, hosted run or YAML library; the workflow is checked structurally against the baseline job text.
